most_relevant.description:
I could not complain having a long layover at the Xiamen Gaoqi International 😊 Arrival and departure areas are labeled in English and in Chinese, and the ground attendants and airport personnel are very helpful when I asked for instructions,  directions and even some trivial questions regarding ATMs, taxi fares and transit hotel. One staff used her mobile translator when I asked a question in English. They did their best to accommodate non-Chinese speaker like myself and I appreciate the gesture. It's not a very huge airport so it's so easy to navigate and the dining options are limited to what I thought is smart not to overwhelm the passengers. There are also  duty-free and convenience stores for the last minute shopping. In all honesty,  I will consider a long layover at this airport again in the future.

This airport is the hub for Xiamen Air and there are benefits when your layover is longer than 8 hours. There are choices for a free transit hotel, lounge or a free city tour. (March 11, 2026)

This review has been edited to add additional info on April 13, 2026 upon  my return to Canada via Xiamen for the 2nd time 😊 My layover is shorter this time and I decided to try the passengers lounge complement of Xiamen Air. I had to pass through customs and immigration to get to the lounge. There is a quiet, dimly lit area in the back for sleeping and there's a shower, as well. However, no towels were provided. I was able to get a good rest and a shower prior to boarding. There's limited choices for dining but Impression Adai is highly recommended for its delicious dishes and remarkable service. Burger King is also located adjacent to Gate 9 if you fancy a burger.

We recently had a layover at Xiamen Airport, and I was genuinely impressed by how smooth and comfortable the whole experience was. The airport was very clean, modern, and well-organized, which made it easy to find my way around even during a short transit. The staff were polite and helpful.

What I appreciated most was how relaxing the atmosphere felt during the layover. There were plenty of seating areas, clean restrooms, and a good variety of shops and food options to explore while waiting for my next flight. The airport had a calm and pleasant environment that made traveling feel less stressful. Overall, Xiamen Airport left a really positive impression on me, and I’d honestly be happy to transit there again in the future.

Overall an okay experience being stuck in Terminal 3 with a few places to eat but very little to do. My two major gripes are that one, while free wifi at the airport is available, they want you to give photos and scan your passport. I find this not only inconvenient but also highly intrusive and suspicious. So unfortunately, I had zero internet access while there. Additionally, having to go through a security check while having been on a 14hr flight is annoying in itself but something I am use to. My problem is how unbelievably SLOW it was. I had probably 50 people ahead of me and it took over an hour to get through. I have never experienced such a snails pace security for simple connecting flights. Due to this, I did not have time to go to any of the lounges I have access to where I could have ate, had a drink and gotten wifi access. Again, the experience was fine but fix the above issues please.

Arrival flow was good and not too much international flight so the immigration was not having long queue. The design of the baggage conveyor belt having the luggage’s falling from top is in my opinion not a good design, it’s impacting the baggage’s and tends to damage things. However for departure it’s is not making sense if you’re flying international in the morning. The airport has a weird design that you will need to go through customs before going into checkin area for international flight. The customs only open at 6:10am so if you have a flight departing at 8am basically you have tight schedule but they don’t care. I had flight at 8:50am and came here around 5:30am to see a super long queue waiting for the customs. The good thing is that the airport is small so we can reach our boarding gate on time.

Extremely inefficient airport. If you are doing International/domestic second leg transfer via this Xiamen Gaoqi Airport, you have to get out of the boarding area, then recheck-in via normal check-in counter even when you had previously checked-in and that your luggage was already checked-in to final destination during your first leg check-in. Then after getting your 2nd leg boarding pass, you go through security screen with everyone else as if you are not doing a transfer.

Very bad experience in here.
Airport amenities and staff attitude all bad, They are not friendly and helpful since i was in here. Most of the staff are so rude,  maybe they have more improvement. They have Free-Wifi but it doesn’t work.

The immigration are so long and a lot of ask, even i only transit a few hours.

The staff's English communication is not good, even though this is an international airport, where the staff should be able to speak English, even if only a little.

When i arrived at the airport, I just found out that free transit hotels are no longer provided for asia to asia layovers (still available for flights starting/ending in china/europe,  The airport is not layover-friendly: WiFi login is difficult, the basement free lounge fills up fast, and Xiamen Air’s own lounge closes at 10pm.

The passport control is usually alright, but the security check is slow, nerve-wracking and cumbersome. I wouldn’t recommend it. Very disappointed.

nice and clean, not too many shops. security a bit clueless. had a flight delayed 24 hours, called xiamen airlines on the phone, they said people at the airport would take care of it. landed in xiamen late at night, and the 24 hour customer support desk was closed. went to the security guys in the booth, he kept asking for a visa, told him about the 24 hour delay, and he had no clue what to do, kept sending us to another security guy. finally a xiamen airlines agent showed up. Very nice lady, after she got our info, got us temp visas, luggage storage, set us up with airline hotel, showed us atm, and help us grab a taxi (only the hotel was free, everything else was at our expense). A bit tedious, spent almost 2 hours getting everything done. this was late at night, maybe 10 passengers at the airport stuck with us, imagine if there was a crowd. Big props to the Agent, she didn't speak any english, we just google translated our way through the whole process lol, but she made sure we were good, even went outside to check on our taxi. We had 2 taxis, one of the taxi's dropped off my mate a block away (he had to walk lol).

the stopover was very nice. Hotel room was nice, but wifi was terrible, ended up buying a 24 hour e-sim from phone app. Xiamen island is very beautiful. the local people were very friendly, especially when i tried to speak Mandarin to them. We went to out of the way places, and not all the shop owners spoke english. My limited mandarin gave the shop owners a good laugh. Ended up being a lovely experience.

went back to the airport, went a little too early, not much to do pre-security. After security, spent an hour at an airport bar at international terminal. the bartender spoke english very well. tried some very flavorful craft beers. I wouldn't mind turning it into a real vacation destination (as long as you don't have any flight delays lol).
beautiful airport with great souvenirs, but very long queue time for international transfer and rigorous security screening. otherwise very smooth and a great layover!

- Xiamen Airlines Transit Lounge Desk: Situated on the basement level of Terminal 3.
- Hotel & Tourism Information Desk: Positioned at the west end of the Domestic Arrival Terminal. \(https://www.xiamenair.com/\)

text_blocks.snippet: Official airport layout and terminal guides for Xiamen Gaoqi International Airport (XMN) are hosted natively on the Official Xiamen Airport Website.
The airport operates two active passenger terminals (Terminal 3 and Terminal 4), which are physically separated by about 4 kilometers.

list.snippet: Terminal 3 (T3): You can access localized diagrams and flight guides through the China Airline Travel T3 Map. T3 spans two main floors (1F Arrivals, 2F Departures) and is the primary hub handling all international flights, regional routes (Hong Kong, Macau, Taiwan), as well as domestic flights operated by XiamenAir, China Southern Airlines, and Hebei Airlines.

Terminal 4 (T4): Detailed structural breakdowns are available on the China Airline Travel T4 Map. T4 operates on a similar two-level configuration (1F Arrivals, 2F Departures) and exclusively processes domestic flights for all other airlines (such as Sichuan Airlines, Shandong Airlines, and Spring Airlines).
Airlines & Services: For individual airline locations and passenger lounges, you can view the complete ANA Xiamen Airport Facility Guide or check the wider InMapz Interactive Airport Directory.

text_blocks.snippet: If you need to transfer between buildings, a free inter-terminal shuttle bus connects T3 (Gate 7) and T4 (Gate 5). The trip takes about 10 minutes and runs every 20 minutes from 5:10 AM to 10:00 PM.
⚠️ Note: All civilian operations at Gaoqi International Airport are scheduled to transition to the newly constructed Xiamen Xiang'an International Airport.
If you are traveling soon, let me know:

list.snippet: Your airline or flight number so I can confirm your exact terminal

sanitizedResponse.reconstructed_markdown:
Official airport layout and terminal guides for Xiamen Gaoqi International Airport \(XMN\) are hosted natively on the [Official Xiamen Airport Website](http://www.xiamenairport.com.cn/).

The airport operates two active passenger terminals \(Terminal 3 and Terminal 4\), which are physically separated by about 4 kilometers. \(https://www.chinaairlinetravel.com/\)

### 🗺️ Terminal Overview & Maps

- Terminal 3 \(T3\): You can access localized diagrams and flight guides through the China Airline Travel T3 Map. T3 spans two main floors \(1F Arrivals, 2F Departures\) and is the primary hub handling all international flights, regional routes \(Hong Kong, Macau, Taiwan\), as well as domestic flights operated by [XiamenAir](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Xiamen_Gaoqi_International_Airport), China Southern Airlines, and Hebei Airlines. \(https://www.chinaairlinetravel.com/\)
- Terminal 4 \(T4\): Detailed structural breakdowns are available on the China Airline Travel T4 Map. T4 operates on a similar two\-level configuration \(1F Arrivals, 2F Departures\) and exclusively processes domestic flights for all other airlines \(such as Sichuan Airlines, Shandong Airlines, and Spring Airlines\). \(https://www.kayak.com/\)
- Airlines & Services: For individual airline locations and passenger lounges, you can view the complete [ANA Xiamen Airport Facility Guide](https://www.ana.co.jp/en/jp/guide/prepare/airport-guide/international/xmn.html) or check the wider [InMapz Interactive Airport Directory](https://maps.inmapz.com/xmn-xiamen-gaoqi-international-airport-859771606-cheung-hei-107085824.269861).

### 🚌 Inter\-Terminal Transfers

If you need to transfer between buildings, a free inter\-terminal shuttle bus connects T3 \(Gate 7\) and T4 \(Gate 5\). The trip takes about 10 minutes and runs every 20 minutes from 5:10 AM to 10:00 PM. \(https://www.trip.com/\)

⚠️ Note: All civilian operations at Gaoqi International Airport are scheduled to transition to the newly constructed Xiamen Xiang'an International Airport. \(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Xiamen\_Gaoqi\_International\_Airport\)

If you are traveling soon, let me know:

- Your airline or flight number so I can confirm your exact terminal
- If you need specific information regarding baggage storage, transit hotels, or ground transportation to downtown Xiamen
